title.narrative: Addressing Youth Needs in Rapidly Transforming Societies

description.narrative:
This workplan supports UNESCO Phnom Penh's contribution to the Bangkok Office's regional strategy for South-East Asia, "Harnessing the power of the social and human sciences to shape inclusive, sustainable, and just societies in South-East Asia," with a focus on positioning youth as agents of change in the context of Cambodia's rapid digital and social transformation. Building on the Cambodia RAM report, the workplan addresses youth's evolving needs in the digital economy and civic life, with a particular emphasis on the ethics of artificial intelligence for youth-led entrepreneurship, intergenerational dialogue on social cohesion and historical memory, and youth leadership in national digital governance processes.
The workplan is delivered through three activity streams: youth-led application of UNESCO's Ethical Impact Assessment tool within youth-led micro, small, and medium enterprises; a youth-organized intergenerational dialogue series on social cohesion and historical memory; and continued support to the Cambodia Youth Internet Governance Forum. It engages youth-led organizations, MSMEs, civil society, and relevant government and technical partners, including the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, the Cambodia Academy of Digital Technology, and Open Development Cambodia.
The workplan contributes to Output 6.4.SHS "Capacities of youth stakeholders strengthened, knowledge generated and youth actions, networks and spaces supported to develop and implement youth-focused policies and programmes addressing multidimensional societal challenges faced by youth" through its support to knowledge production on and by youth (C/5 indicator 6.4.SHS.1), supporting youth stakeholders in shaping digital governance dialogue (C/5 indicator 6.4.SHS.2), and supporting youth-led action and innovation on social issues (C/5 indicator 6.4.SHS.3).
